acquisition_method: Data was acquired in a DDA (data dependent acquisition) mode using a top15 method with a 150 min runtime.
alkylation_concentration: NK cells were lysed in SDS lysis buffer (4% SDS, 10 mM TCEP and 50 mM TEAB), alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetemide and processed using the SP3 method as previously described (Marchingo JM et. al., 2020 doi: 10.7554/eLife.53725).
alkylation_reagent: NK cells were lysed in SDS lysis buffer (4% SDS, 10 mM TCEP and 50 mM TEAB), alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetemide and processed using the SP3 method as previously described (Marchingo JM et. al., 2020 doi: 10.7554/eLife.53725).
cleavage_agent: Peptides were digested overnight with LysC then trypsin in a 1:100 ratio.
fractionation_method: For fractionsation, peptides were adjusted to 5% formic acid and separated into 16 fractions by high pH reverse phase HPLC using an UltiMate 3000 HPLC system on a 2.1 mm x 150 mm XBridge Peptide BEH C18 column with 3.5 μm particles (Waters) column.
ionization_type: Following separation, peptides were electrosprayed by an Easy-Spray source set at 50ºC and source voltage 2.0 kV to a Q-Exactive Plus Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Scientific), which was operated in positive ion mode.
reduction_concentration: NK cells were lysed in SDS lysis buffer (4% SDS, 10 mM TCEP and 50 mM TEAB), alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetemide and processed using the SP3 method as previously described (Marchingo JM et. al., 2020 doi: 10.7554/eLife.53725).
reduction_reagent: NK cells were lysed in SDS lysis buffer (4% SDS, 10 mM TCEP and 50 mM TEAB), alkylated with 20 mM iodoacetemide and processed using the SP3 method as previously described (Marchingo JM et. al., 2020 doi: 10.7554/eLife.53725).

instrument.evidence: Following separation, peptides were electrosprayed by an Easy-Spray source set at 50ºC and source voltage 2.0 kV to a Q-Exactive Plus Mass Spectrometer (Thermo Scientific), which was operated in positive ion mode.

ptm.value: carbamidomethylation, oxidation, acetylation, deamination, N-terminal conversion of glutamine to pyro-glutamic acid
ptm.evidence: Cysteine carbamidomethylation was included as a fixed modification and methionine oxidation, protein N-terminal acetylation, deamination of asparagine and glutamine and N-terminal conversion of glutamine to pyro-glutamic acid were included as variable modifications.
